title: Secure Mobile Access to SharePoint Online under MAM (App Protection + Conditional Access)
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (multi-component: App Protection Policies + Conditional Access + supported access paths + intranet-routing/Microsoft Tunnel-for-MAM decision + root-cause diagnostics; live-access risk).

Doubles as the resolution to a real support case: employees can't reliably reach a SharePoint Online intranet from mobile under a MAM configuration. Keep customer/intranet names OUT (white-label). version_directive: New; branding: off.
hook: Make SharePoint Online reliably reachable on mobile under MAM — without breaking data protection
problem: A SharePoint Online intranet that works fine on a laptop can be a mess on mobile the moment Mobile Application Management (MAM) is in play: employees get blocked or bounced, links open in the wrong app, and productivity stalls. The cause is almost always a mismatch between App Protection Policies, Conditional Access, and the access path the user actually takes (the SharePoint mobile app vs. a protected browser) — and sometimes an intranet-routing gap. This solution gives you the correct, repeatable way to deliver secure, reliable mobile access to SharePoint Online under MAM in Microsoft Intune, and a diagnostic path to root-cause when it isn't working.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — how mobile access to SharePoint Online works under MAM, the interplay of App Protection Policies + Conditional Access, the supported access paths (the SharePoint mobile app vs. a MAM-protected browser like Edge), and when intranet routing / Microsoft Tunnel for MAM is required.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Intune with App Protection, Entra ID + Conditional Access, the Microsoft 365 apps in scope, licensing, target user groups, a pilot group) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide (the resolution) — exact, ordered steps: define the App Protection Policies, build the Conditional Access policy (approved client apps / app-protection grant), confirm the supported access path and steer users to it, decide and (if needed) wire intranet routing / Tunnel for MAM, validate mobile access end to end, then pilot and expand.

Root-cause diagnostic tree — a step-by-step method for 'can't access the intranet on mobile': CA block vs. missing app-protection grant vs. wrong access path (browser vs. app) vs. routing/Tunnel gap vs. sign-in/token issues, with how to confirm each.

5 PowerShell scripts — App Protection + Conditional Access readiness discovery, per-user mobile-access validation, an access + policy-coverage report, safe remediation of misconfigured assignments, and a mobile-access scope-group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.
short: The correct, repeatable way to deliver secure, reliable mobile access to SharePoint Online under MAM — App Protection Policies + Conditional Access + the right access path (SharePoint app vs. protected browser) + the intranet-routing decision, with a root-cause diagnostic tree. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
